translation:
With the hidden (fu) pulse, the five depressions (wu yu) are already known first; wood likes free reaching-abundance, urgently emesis it. Fire burning upward must be sweated out; earth (spleen) delights in stagnation, seizing (purging) it is marvelous.
Metal of itself is clear and empty — what is it clogged? Water's nature rushes and flows — break (unblock) it, do not delay. Blood, qi, damp-heat, phlegm and food are also named the six depressions (liu yu), one must know.
The ascending does not ascend, the descending does not descend; when it should transform and does not transform, it loses its season. The root causes of all depressions begin from this; Jieyu Tang (Resolve-Depression Decoction) head is the mechanism of creation.
Jieyu (Resolve-depression) with Xiangfu (Cyperus), Cangzhu (Atractylodes) and Chuanxiong; Chenpi (Tangerine), Shenqu (Medicated Leaven), Baifu (Poria) following. Beimu (Fritillaria), Lianqiao (Forsythia), Zhizi (Gardenia), Sugeng (Perilla stem) and Zhi (Zhike/Bitter Orange); again the state elder (Guolao=licorice) labors within it.
translator_notes: 五鬱=the five depressions (wood fire earth metal water); 六鬱=six depressions.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
The illnesses made by phlegm cannot all be spoken; the thick is phlegm, the thin is rheum (yin) in detail. Regulating qi to treat the branch is a quick method, though; fortifying the spleen to treat the root is even better.
How does one recognize the coming of the all conditions? Each hue, at the edge of the stream, is floating or sinking. Erchen (Two-Matured) formulas, when signs appear, must be increased or decreased; Gunan Tan (Roll-the-Phlegm Beverage) used, think carefully.
Erchen (Two-Matured) with Gancao (Licorice) and Chenpi (Tangerine Peel); Banxia (Pinellia) and Fuling (Poria) with skin removed. In the phlegm-cough battle formation it is the supreme general; adding soldiers and reducing cook-fires, it brings back spring.

Now phlegm is the thief of the human heart. Born in the spleen and stomach, unable to move of itself, it follows qi and little by little grows. Now in treating phlegm, one must first regulate qi; this statement being surely the correct treatment-of-branch theory. Without strengthening and removing dampness it is not the complete treatment-of-root. In this formula Banxia, pungent and warm, can dry dampness; Fuling, sweet and pale, can percolate dampness; dampness removed, phlegm has no rebirth. Chenpi, warm, can free the qi; Gancao, pungent and level, can benefit the spleen. Erchen not only treats phlegm, it can make the stool moist, the urine long.
translator_notes: 二陳湯=Erchen Tang (Two-Matured Decoction); 滾痰飲=Gunan Tan.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
The lung is the canopied canopy, named clear and empty; suddenly it is invaded by an evil spirit entering its abode. Sound without phlegm comes as a dry cough (ke); no sound with phlegm, a productive cough (sou), hard to remove.
With sound and with phlegm it is cough (kesou), making one's five viscera restless without rest. Shensu (Ginseng-Perilla) follows the four seasons, adding and subtracting; Dingxiang Banxia (Clove and Pinellia) made into pills is required.
Within Shensu Yin (Ginseng-Perilla Beverage) are Zhiqiao (Bitter Orange) and Qianhu (Peucedanum); Banxia (Pinellia), Chenpi (Tangerine), Jiegeng (Platycodon) and Lu (Lugen/Reed Rhizome). Gancao (Licorice), Fuling (Poria) and Muxiang (Aucklandia) as powder; clearing metal (lung) and draining fire, all the illnesses are dredged free.

Dingxiang Banxia Wan (Clove and Pinellia Pill)
Renshen (Ginseng), Ganjiang (Dried Ginger), Dingxiang (Clove), Xixin (Asarum), Banxia (Pinellia), Binglang (Areca)

When the spleen and stomach are warm, then it can transport and move; with phlegm-rheum, the spleen and stomach being deficient and cold, then phlegm-rheum stops in the chest and diaphragm, and the lung qi thereby becomes unruly, and is then made to cough. The pungency of Banxia is that which dries the spleen; the sweet of Renshen is that which nourishes the stomach. The warmth of Ganjiang is that which moves the phlegm. The pungency of Xixin is that which disperses the rheum. Using Binglang takes its heavy nature, able to follow the phlegm. The Classics say that which is high should be pressed down — such is this.
translator_notes: 參蘇飲=Shensu Yin; 丁香半夏丸=Dingxiang Banxia Wan.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
